---
title: "Job"
---

# Job

::: {.book-summary}
## Book Summary Insight

Job explores the mystery of suffering, the sovereignty of God, and the limits of human understanding. The book teaches that God's wisdom and purposes transcend human comprehension and remain worthy of trust.
:::

::: {.chapter-entry}
## Chapter 1

<div class="key-verse">Job 1:21</div>

<div class="identifier">The LORD gave, and the LORD hath taken away</div>

### Why This Verse

Job's response to loss

### Chapter Insight

This chapter introduces Job's righteousness and his sudden suffering. The key verse demonstrates unwavering worship despite devastating loss.
:::

::: {.chapter-entry}
## Chapter 2

<div class="key-verse">Job 2:10</div>

<div class="identifier">Shall we receive good and not evil?</div>

### Why This Verse

Job's perseverance

### Chapter Insight

This chapter records Job's physical affliction and continued faithfulness. The key verse highlights perseverance when suffering intensifies.
:::

::: {.chapter-entry}
## Chapter 3

<div class="key-verse">Job 3:3</div>

<div class="identifier">Let the day perish wherein I was born</div>

### Why This Verse

Beginning of Job's lament

### Chapter Insight

This chapter contains Job's lament over his suffering. The key verse expresses the depth of human anguish and confusion.
:::

::: {.chapter-entry}
## Chapter 4

<div class="key-verse">Job 4:8</div>

<div class="identifier">They that plow iniquity reap the same</div>

### Why This Verse

Eliphaz's theology

### Chapter Insight

This chapter begins Eliphaz's first speech. The key verse reflects the mistaken belief that suffering is always the result of personal sin.
:::

::: {.chapter-entry}
## Chapter 5

<div class="key-verse">Job 5:17</div>

<div class="identifier">Happy is the man whom God correcteth</div>

### Why This Verse

Later quoted in Hebrews

### Chapter Insight

This chapter continues Eliphaz's counsel. The key verse emphasizes God's discipline, though applied incorrectly to Job's situation.
:::

::: {.chapter-entry}
## Chapter 6

<div class="key-verse">Job 6:24</div>

<div class="identifier">Teach me, and I will hold my tongue</div>

### Why This Verse

Job seeks understanding

### Chapter Insight

This chapter records Job's response to Eliphaz. The key verse reveals Job's desire for understanding and compassion amid suffering.
:::

::: {.chapter-entry}
## Chapter 7

<div class="key-verse">Job 7:17</div>

<div class="identifier">What is man, that Thou shouldest magnify him?</div>

### Why This Verse

Famous reflection on humanity

### Chapter Insight

This chapter expresses Job's weariness and questions. The key verse highlights the brevity and difficulty of life.
:::

::: {.chapter-entry}
## Chapter 8

<div class="key-verse">Job 8:7</div>

<div class="identifier">Though thy beginning was small</div>

### Why This Verse

Frequently quoted encouragement

### Chapter Insight

This chapter contains Bildad's first speech. The key verse reflects confidence in traditional wisdom while misunderstanding Job's circumstances.
:::

::: {.chapter-entry}
## Chapter 9

<div class="key-verse">Job 9:2</div>

<div class="identifier">How should man be just with God?</div>

### Why This Verse

Central theological question

### Chapter Insight

This chapter records Job's recognition of God's greatness. The key verse expresses humanity's need for a mediator before God.
:::

::: {.chapter-entry}
## Chapter 10

<div class="key-verse">Job 10:12</div>

<div class="identifier">Thou hast granted me life and favor</div>

### Why This Verse

Job recalls God's care

### Chapter Insight

This chapter continues Job's plea for understanding. The key verse reveals his struggle to reconcile suffering with God's purposes.
:::

::: {.chapter-entry}
## Chapter 11

<div class="key-verse">Job 11:7</div>

<div class="identifier">Canst thou by searching find out God?</div>

### Why This Verse

Zophar's challenge

### Chapter Insight

This chapter contains Zophar's first speech. The key verse demonstrates the limitations of human understanding about God's ways.
:::

::: {.chapter-entry}
## Chapter 12

<div class="key-verse">Job 12:13</div>

<div class="identifier">With Him are wisdom and strength</div>

### Why This Verse

God's sovereignty

### Chapter Insight

This chapter begins Job's response to his friends. The key verse affirms God's sovereignty over all creation.
:::

::: {.chapter-entry}
## Chapter 13

<div class="key-verse">Job 13:15</div>

<div class="identifier">Though He slay me, yet will I trust Him</div>

### Why This Verse

One of Job's most quoted verses

### Chapter Insight

This chapter records Job's determination to trust God. The key verse expresses remarkable faith despite uncertainty.
:::

::: {.chapter-entry}
## Chapter 14

<div class="key-verse">Job 14:14</div>

<div class="identifier">If a man die, shall he live again?</div>

### Why This Verse

Hope beyond death

### Chapter Insight

This chapter reflects on the frailty of human life. The key verse expresses hope beyond death.
:::

::: {.chapter-entry}
## Chapter 15

<div class="key-verse">Job 15:35</div>

<div class="identifier">They conceive mischief and bring forth vanity</div>

### Why This Verse

Eliphaz's accusation

### Chapter Insight

This chapter contains Eliphaz's second speech. The key verse continues the argument that suffering proves guilt.
:::

::: {.chapter-entry}
## Chapter 16

<div class="key-verse">Job 16:19</div>

<div class="identifier">My witness is in heaven</div>

### Why This Verse

Job's appeal

### Chapter Insight

This chapter records Job's complaint against his friends. The key verse reveals his longing for an advocate in heaven.
:::

::: {.chapter-entry}
## Chapter 17

<div class="key-verse">Job 17:9</div>

<div class="identifier">The righteous shall hold on his way</div>

### Why This Verse

Perseverance

### Chapter Insight

This chapter expresses Job's discouragement. The key verse highlights the struggle to maintain hope amid despair.
:::

::: {.chapter-entry}
## Chapter 18

<div class="key-verse">Job 18:21</div>

<div class="identifier">Such are the dwellings of the wicked</div>

### Why This Verse

Bildad's conclusion

### Chapter Insight

This chapter contains Bildad's second speech. The key verse reflects his conviction that the wicked inevitably suffer judgment.
:::

::: {.chapter-entry}
## Chapter 19

<div class="key-verse">Job 19:25</div>

<div class="identifier">I know that my Redeemer liveth</div>

### Why This Verse

Most famous verse in Job

### Chapter Insight

This chapter records Job's declaration of faith. The key verse expresses hope in a living Redeemer despite present suffering.
:::

::: {.chapter-entry}
## Chapter 20

<div class="key-verse">Job 20:5</div>

<div class="identifier">The triumphing of the wicked is short</div>

### Why This Verse

Zophar's argument

### Chapter Insight

This chapter contains Zophar's second speech. The key verse emphasizes the temporary nature of wicked prosperity.
:::

::: {.chapter-entry}
## Chapter 21

<div class="key-verse">Job 21:7</div>

<div class="identifier">Why do the wicked live?</div>

### Why This Verse

Job challenges conventional wisdom

### Chapter Insight

This chapter challenges simplistic views of suffering. The key verse observes that the wicked often prosper despite their rebellion.
:::

::: {.chapter-entry}
## Chapter 22

<div class="key-verse">Job 22:21</div>

<div class="identifier">Acquaint now thyself with Him, and be at peace</div>

### Why This Verse

Widely quoted counsel

### Chapter Insight

This chapter contains Eliphaz's final speech. The key verse urges repentance, though wrongly assuming Job's guilt.
:::

::: {.chapter-entry}
## Chapter 23

<div class="key-verse">Job 23:10</div>

<div class="identifier">When He has tried me, I shall come forth as gold</div>

### Why This Verse

Classic faith-under-trial verse

### Chapter Insight

This chapter records Job's longing to present his case before God. The key verse expresses confidence in God's ultimate vindication.
:::

::: {.chapter-entry}
## Chapter 24

<div class="key-verse">Job 24:1</div>

<div class="identifier">Why are times not hidden from the Almighty?</div>

### Why This Verse

Justice questioned

### Chapter Insight

This chapter wrestles with apparent injustice in the world. The key verse questions why evil often goes unpunished.
:::

::: {.chapter-entry}
## Chapter 25

<div class="key-verse">Job 25:6</div>

<div class="identifier">Man is a worm</div>

### Why This Verse

Bildad's humility theme

### Chapter Insight

This chapter contains Bildad's final remarks. The key verse emphasizes God's holiness and human weakness.
:::

::: {.chapter-entry}
## Chapter 26

<div class="key-verse">Job 26:7</div>

<div class="identifier">He hangs the earth upon nothing</div>

### Why This Verse

Frequently cited scientific-sounding statement

### Chapter Insight

This chapter celebrates God's majesty in creation. The key verse highlights the vastness of God's power beyond human comprehension.
:::

::: {.chapter-entry}
## Chapter 27

<div class="key-verse">Job 27:5</div>

<div class="identifier">Till I die I will not remove mine integrity</div>

### Why This Verse

Job's resolve

### Chapter Insight

This chapter records Job's continued defense of his integrity. The key verse demonstrates his commitment to righteousness.
:::

::: {.chapter-entry}
## Chapter 28

<div class="key-verse">Job 28:28</div>

<div class="identifier">The fear of the Lord, that is wisdom</div>

### Why This Verse

One of Job's great themes

### Chapter Insight

This chapter reflects on the nature of true wisdom. The key verse identifies reverence for God as the source of wisdom.
:::

::: {.chapter-entry}
## Chapter 29

<div class="key-verse">Job 29:14</div>

<div class="identifier">I put on righteousness</div>

### Why This Verse

Job remembers former honor

### Chapter Insight

This chapter recalls Job's former blessings and influence. The key verse highlights the respect and honor he once enjoyed.
:::

::: {.chapter-entry}
## Chapter 30

<div class="key-verse">Job 30:20</div>

<div class="identifier">I cry unto Thee, and Thou dost not hear</div>

### Why This Verse

Job's anguish

### Chapter Insight

This chapter contrasts Job's past honor with present suffering. The key verse expresses the depth of his humiliation.
:::

::: {.chapter-entry}
## Chapter 31

<div class="key-verse">Job 31:1</div>

<div class="identifier">I made a covenant with mine eyes</div>

### Why This Verse

Frequently quoted purity verse

### Chapter Insight

This chapter presents Job's final defense. The key verse demonstrates his commitment to personal integrity before God.
:::

::: {.chapter-entry}
## Chapter 32

<div class="key-verse">Job 32:8</div>

<div class="identifier">There is a spirit in man</div>

### Why This Verse

Elihu begins speaking

### Chapter Insight

This chapter introduces Elihu. The key verse highlights the importance of speaking with humility and discernment.
:::

::: {.chapter-entry}
## Chapter 33

<div class="key-verse">Job 33:4</div>

<div class="identifier">The Spirit of God hath made me</div>

### Why This Verse

Creation and life

### Chapter Insight

This chapter contains Elihu's appeal to Job. The key verse emphasizes God's desire to communicate and redeem.
:::

::: {.chapter-entry}
## Chapter 34

<div class="key-verse">Job 34:10</div>

<div class="identifier">Far be it from God to do wickedness</div>

### Why This Verse

Elihu on divine justice

### Chapter Insight

This chapter defends God's justice. The key verse affirms that God always acts righteously.
:::

::: {.chapter-entry}
## Chapter 35

<div class="key-verse">Job 35:10</div>

<div class="identifier">Where is God my Maker?</div>

### Why This Verse

Seeking God in suffering

### Chapter Insight

This chapter discusses human righteousness and God's transcendence. The key verse highlights God's independence from human actions.
:::

::: {.chapter-entry}
## Chapter 36

<div class="key-verse">Job 36:26</div>

<div class="identifier">God is great, and we know Him not</div>

### Why This Verse

Divine transcendence

### Chapter Insight

This chapter continues Elihu's defense of God's ways. The key verse emphasizes God's greatness and wisdom.
:::

::: {.chapter-entry}
## Chapter 37

<div class="key-verse">Job 37:14</div>

<div class="identifier">Stand still and consider the wondrous works of God</div>

### Why This Verse

Preparation for God's appearance

### Chapter Insight

This chapter points to God's majesty in nature. The key verse prepares the reader for God's direct response.
:::

::: {.chapter-entry}
## Chapter 38

<div class="key-verse">Job 38:4</div>

<div class="identifier">Where wast thou when I laid the foundations of the earth?</div>

### Why This Verse

God's first challenge

### Chapter Insight

This chapter begins God's answer from the whirlwind. The key verse demonstrates the limits of human understanding compared to God's wisdom.
:::

::: {.chapter-entry}
## Chapter 39

<div class="key-verse">Job 39:19</div>

<div class="identifier">Hast thou given the horse strength?</div>

### Why This Verse

God's wisdom in creation

### Chapter Insight

This chapter continues God's questions concerning creation. The key verse emphasizes God's care and governance over all creatures.
:::

::: {.chapter-entry}
## Chapter 40

<div class="key-verse">Job 40:4</div>

<div class="identifier">Behold, I am vile; what shall I answer Thee?</div>

### Why This Verse

Job's humility

### Chapter Insight

This chapter calls Job to humility before God. The key verse highlights the inadequacy of challenging God's wisdom.
:::

::: {.chapter-entry}
## Chapter 41

<div class="key-verse">Job 41:1</div>

<div class="identifier">Canst thou draw out Leviathan?</div>

### Why This Verse

Famous Leviathan passage

### Chapter Insight

This chapter describes Leviathan. The key verse demonstrates God's unmatched power over forces beyond human control.
:::

::: {.chapter-entry}
## Chapter 42

<div class="key-verse">Job 42:5</div>

<div class="identifier">I have heard of Thee, but now mine eye seeth Thee</div>

### Why This Verse

Job's final realization

### Chapter Insight

This chapter records Job's repentance, restoration, and vindication. The key verse reveals true wisdom through humility before God.
:::
